content:
Ethan Park: quick RBAC question on the staged rollouts overrides. We’re adding `force_promote` + `hold` (and later `force_rollback`). What permission(s) should gate these? Right now PR has `dedicated.pools.rollouts.write` for everything.

Benji Okafor: yeah +1. in the control plane I can split it out, just want agreement before we bake names into authz + audit. current endpoints:
- POST /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{plan_id}:promote
- ...:hold
- ...:abort
- ...:forcePromote (bypass gates)

Jordan Lee: from policy engine POV, `force_promote` is materially different bc it overrides the gate eval result + writes “override=true” into the state transition. I’d prefer explicit permission.

Chloe Martin: Console side: we’ll hide the force buttons unless user has a specific perm. also we want to show the warning modal + require a reason string.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: :eyes: please do not reuse generic “write” for overrides. recommend separate permission(s) for:
1) normal stage promotion
2) hold/resume
3) abort
4) bypass gates (force promote/force rollback)
And we should decide whether any customer-admin should EVER have bypass gates.

Rafael Mendes: SRE stance: bypass gates should be Redwood-only. even “hold” could be customer-admin in some cases (they pause while they investigate), but force promote is basically “accept risk / degrade SLO” territory.

Ethan Park: makes sense. question is how we define “Redwood-only” in roles. We have internal operators, and some enterprise customers have “org admin” in Console.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: internal vs external split is the big one. we can do:
- `dedicated.rollouts.promote`
- `dedicated.rollouts.hold`
- `dedicated.rollouts.abort`
- `dedicated.rollouts.override` (force promote/force rollback)
And then bind `override` only to internal roles.

Benji Okafor: what internal role name do we want to use? today we have `platform-admin` (too broad), `sre-oncall`, `fleet-operator`. Dedicated has `dedicated-operator` too.

Priya Natarajan: we should keep roles coarse and perms fine. I’d rather add perms and map to existing internal roles initially. If we need a new role, do it as a follow-up.

Jordan Lee: +1. main thing is API enforces `override` separately so we can reason about audit + compliance. console hiding is not sufficient.

Hannah Rivera: UX detail: “Hold” is also a type of override-ish action (stops auto-promotion) but doesn’t bypass gates. Should be separate perm so customers can pause without giving them bypass.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: exactly. “hold” is reversible + non-destructive. but still a change mgmt action, so it should be permissioned and audited.

Ethan Park: proposal:
Perms:
- `dedicated.rollouts.read` (view plan + gate evidence)
- `dedicated.rollouts.manage` (create/update plan, start rollout)
- `dedicated.rollouts.promote` (promote stage w/ gates enforced)
- `dedicated.rollouts.hold` (hold/resume)
- `dedicated.rollouts.abort` (abort rollout)
- `dedicated.rollouts.override` (force_promote, force_rollback; also “promote w/ gateStatus=UNKNOWN”)

Bind:
- Customer: `read/manage/promote/hold/abort` (TBD if abort allowed)
- Internal: all of above incl override

Thoughts?

Rafael Mendes: I’d be careful giving customers `abort` by default. In incident, customer aborting could race with our remediation. But also they might need it. Maybe allow abort if rollout initiated by that org? (ownership check).

Benji Okafor: ownership check is doable: rollout plan has `created_by_actor_type` + `created_by_org_id`. we can restrict customer abort to plans created by that org, but internal can abort anything.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: that’s good. also for `override`, I want “break-glass” semantics:
- require `reason` string
- optionally require `ticket_url` (Jira/incident)
- emit audit event with old/new stage, gate snapshot, and actor
Even if we don’t hard-require ticket_url in v1, at least accept the field.

Chloe Martin: console can enforce “reason required” client-side, but API should enforce too (non-empty) for override. For normal promote we can accept empty reason.

Jordan Lee: policy engine will store gate eval output at time of decision (pass/fail/unknown + observed metrics window). For override, we should attach the gate snapshot so audit has evidence of what was bypassed.

Ethan Park: ok. naming: do we want `override` or `force`? Security tends to prefer `override` since it’s broader.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: `override` is fine. but make the action explicit in audit: `rollout.force_promote` vs `rollout.promote`.

Benji Okafor: implementation plan:
- authz check in control plane: `override` required when request has `bypass_gates=true` or endpoint is :forcePromote/:forceRollback
- `hold` endpoint checks `dedicated.rollouts.hold`
- `promote` endpoint checks `dedicated.rollouts.promote`
- `abort` checks `dedicated.rollouts.abort` + ownership logic for external actors
- require `reason` for override actions
- wire to audit emitter

Priya Natarajan: sounds good. also make sure service-to-service calls (automation) use a service principal with least perms. do we have an automated “auto-abort on gate fail” job? if yes it needs abort permission.

Jordan Lee: auto-abort is policy engine initiated. it calls control plane with service principal `policy-engine-prod`. It should get `dedicated.rollouts.abort` but NOT `override`.

Rafael Mendes: +1, auto systems should never have override.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: also clarify: “missing metrics fail-closed” means gateStatus=UNKNOWN blocks promote. if someone wants to proceed, that’s an override and should require `dedicated.rollouts.override`.

Hannah Rivera: Console copy: “Gate data missing. Promotion blocked.” then show “Force promote (admin only)” with scary text.

Chloe Martin: and we’ll display who has permissions: “Contact Redwood support / your org admin.” But note: for customer org admin, they still won’t have override. So text should be “Contact Redwood on-call / support” not “org admin”.

Ethan Park: good catch.

Benji Okafor: Kaitlyn can you confirm which internal roles should get `dedicated.rollouts.override` at launch? SRE oncall? Dedicated operator? platform admin?

Kaitlyn Nguyen: recommend: `sre-oncall` + `dedicated-operator` yes. `platform-admin` already has everything but we should avoid making that the only path. Also: require MFA / SSO, but that’s baseline for internal anyway.

Rafael Mendes: we should probably add a runbook step: if using override, paste incident link into reason, and page #dedicated-oncall for visibility. (Even if it’s a customer-driven request.)

Priya Natarajan: :thumbsup: ship with that. Benji please update PR w/ perm split + ownership + reason requirement. Kaitlyn, can you do a quick security sign-off comment once it’s up?

Kaitlyn Nguyen: yes. tag me on the diff. also please ensure audit event includes `actor_type` (user/service), `actor_id`, `org_id` (if external), `override=true/false`, and `override_reason`.

Benji Okafor: will do. I’ll also add a quick note in the API docs so Console/SDK knows which errors map to “missing permission” vs “ownership denied”.

Jordan Lee: last thing: should `hold` be allowed for service principals? (e.g. automation holding on burn?)

Rafael Mendes: not in v1 imo. hold is an operational action; automation should abort on gate fail, not hold.

Ethan Park: ok: service principals get abort only.

Chloe Martin: tracking this in Console ticket too. We’ll add a permissions check endpoint already returning `allowed_actions` per plan; it’ll incorporate these perms.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: cool. thanks all.
